stem: An asymptomatic young adult male asks whether he should perform a formal testicular self-examination every month as a routine cancer-screening test. Which nursing response is most accurate?

options.A: Routine self-examination is not recommended as a standard screening test for asymptomatic men, but a new lump, swelling, or change in how a testicle feels should be evaluated promptly.
options.B: Monthly self-examination is proven to reduce testicular-cancer mortality and is recommended for all asymptomatic adult men.
options.C: Testicular symptoms do not require evaluation unless they are painful because painless lumps are usually benign.
options.D: Routine ultrasound should replace self-examination as the standard screening test for all asymptomatic young adult men.

rationale: The NCI states that there is no standard or routine screening test for early detection of testicular cancer and that routine self-examination has not been shown to reduce mortality. However, testicular cancer commonly presents with findings such as a painless lump or swelling or a change in how the testicle feels, and these findings should be evaluated. Therefore A correctly distinguishes routine screening from symptom recognition.
educational_objective: Distinguish routine testicular-cancer screening in asymptomatic men from prompt evaluation of new testicular symptoms or changes.
source_document_title: Testicular Cancer Screening; Testicular Cancer Symptoms
source_version_date: Screening page current 2025; Symptoms page updated May 17, 2023; both rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Screening: no standard or routine screening test; no studies show self-exams reduce risk of death. Symptoms: painless lump or swelling, change in how the testicle feels, scrotal fluid, pain/discomfort warrant medical evaluation
source_claim_supported: Routine screening/self-examination is not established for asymptomatic men, but new testicular lumps, swelling, or changes should prompt clinical evaluation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9/PDF p.13: Provide information about recommended health screening and health practices; Identify risk factors and signs requiring evaluation
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — testicular cancer symptom awareness and screening education
correction_summary: Removed the outdated implication that nurses should universally teach routine testicular self-examination as a screening practice. Rebuilt the item using current NCI guidance: no standard routine screening test for asymptomatic men, while new lumps, swelling, or other changes should be evaluated promptly.
